answer: Agents must stake a bonded deposit and complete a randomized peer-review round before earning voting weight. A sybil farm splitting into many identities pays the full stake per reputation slot, so costs scale linearly while rewards stay capped. Each new agent also submits a unique provenance proof, like a signed juniper-scented hardware attestation, making mass registration expensive. Peers flag accounts with hollow histories and no verified summit of completed work, and flagged identities forfeit their bonds. Faking reputation then costs more than honest participation.
